reason: Re-opened packet.js gita 3 --verse 3.42. Sankara (Mahadeva Sastri): 'He, the Self, the witness of reason, is superior to reason' stands in his commentary on 3.42, the pronoun read as the Self. Ramanuja (Govindacharya): in the commentary body, not only the translator's footnote 4, 'desire or lust ... will yet assert mastery over all ... That which then is the most strong and overpowering, viz., kama ... is denoted by the pronoun sah'; this is Ramanuja's well-known distinctive reading of sah as kama. Both locators 3.42 right; the paraphrases do not go beyond those words ('of all' carried by 'mastery over all'). Genuine difference named, not resolved, both schools named, no comparison or other tradition in the sentence (the Dhammapada and Omar Khayyam are only in Govindacharya's footnote). Plain sense checked against day.js: 3.36 asks what drags a man to sin, 3.37 to 3.41 name desire the foe, 3.42 ranks senses, mind, Reason and what is beyond; no four words of the verse repeated, no doctrine. Key verse verse.js ok (Bhagavad Gita 3.42, at [160]); entry-check ok, 49 words under the 60 cap for two commentators, src 131 chars. Besant's capital 'He' leans toward the Sankara sense, but the sentence treats it only as the pronoun both commentators gloss, and Telang's 3.42 also ends with the bare pronoun. Operator note confirmed: recheck-evidence.js squash() applies /<[^>]+>/ to the whole packet haystack, so the Sankara piece will likely report NOT FOUND for a tool reason; the words are in the packet as printed.
